ACME Insight is here: operational analytics on data you already trust.

JK
Jana Kovář — Co-founder & CEO
May 7, 2026 · 8 min read

After two years in private beta with twenty-three customers, ACME Insight is now generally available to every Pro and Enterprise account. It's the third — and we suspect final — pillar of the suite. We held the launch six months longer than the roadmap said we would, and that's most of what this post is about.

The pitch is straightforward: operational analytics built on the platform your team already trusts. Same data model. Same audit trail. Same permissions. No CSV exports, no separate BI tool, no four-week onboarding from a different vendor. You enable Insight, you point it at your existing workflows, and you get dashboards in roughly an hour.

Why we waited

The temptation in our position — a profitable platform company with a long customer waitlist — is to ship adjacent products on the original momentum and figure out the details later. We've watched several peers do exactly this, and we've watched their NPS scores reflect it.

We held Insight back for three reasons:

  1. The first version benchmarked against industry data, which sounded great in marketing materials and turned out to be useless in practice. Customers wanted to compare themselves to their own historical baselines, not to anonymized peers in adjacent verticals.
  2. Anomaly detection in v1 generated four times more alerts than we'd projected. We had to rebuild the model from scratch around a confidence-weighted approach that surfaces the things actually worth a human's attention.
  3. The permissions model didn't extend cleanly. Insight surfaced data that some viewers shouldn't have seen, and the fix required changes to the underlying platform — not just the new product.
Lesson from v1

Industry benchmarks make great marketing copy and lousy product. The most compelling comparison isn't to other companies — it's to last quarter's version of yourself. We rebuilt around that insight and the entire product made more sense.

What's in the box

The GA release ships with everything our beta cohort told us was non-negotiable, and a few things we added in the final stretch:

  • Real-time dashboards across workflow throughput, exception rates, cycle times, and SLA adherence — built on the same data layer as Core and Flow, no ETL required
  • Anomaly detection with configurable confidence thresholds; alerts route through your existing notification channels
  • Historical benchmarking against your own data — month-over-month, quarter-over-quarter, year-over-year, with seasonality adjustment
  • Custom metric builder for the operational KPIs that don't fit our standard library
  • Scheduled reporting — the same dashboards, delivered as branded PDFs to your board or your customer's compliance team

What we learned about beta cohorts

Twenty-three customers turned out to be exactly the right number. Twelve would have been too few — we wouldn't have caught the edge cases. Forty would have been too many — we couldn't have responded fast enough to the patterns we were seeing.

"The beta wasn't a feature freeze. It was the first six months of the product's life, with the right group of people telling us what was actually broken."

The beta program ran on a simple deal: customers got Insight at no charge for the duration of the program, and committed to a weekly thirty-minute call with the product team. We honored that commitment on both sides. The product is materially better for it.

What's next for Insight

Two themes for the rest of 2026: natural-language query ("show me last month's exception rate by team") and predictive operations — using your historical patterns to surface what's likely to break before it does. Both are in early prototyping. We'll publish more once we know they work.

If you're already on Pro or Enterprise, Insight is in your dashboard now. If you're not — well, you know where the contact page is.

— Jana
